For each step, calculate world position $p = ro + rd \cdot t$, sample the combined scene $d = \text{map}(p)$, check for intersection if $d.x < \epsilon$ (e.g., $0.001$), and advance $t \leftarrow t + d.x$ otherwise [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately describes the raymarching algorithm presented in Source [S1]. The source code explicitly defines the world position calculation as `p = ro + rd * t`, samples the combined scene using `d = map(p)` where `map` returns a `float2`, checks for intersection using the condition `if (d.x < 0.001)`, and advances the step size using `t += d.x` (implied by the standard raymarching loop structure where `t` is incremented by the distance `d.x` when no hit is detected, as seen in the logic flow of the provided code snippet). All specific details in the claim are present in the evidence.
